headline: High: shared browser/MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is limited by missing residency data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers and use MCP, so it may ingest untrusted web or file content; Agent B exposes a REST API and broad egress, so A’s outputs could be bridged into B through orchestration. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed, but the pathway exists in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF Agent A ingests browser content or MCP payloads as instructions
IF an orchestrator forwards A output into Agent B inputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable browser-to-agent instruction following for untrusted pages
Add provenance tags to MCP and REST payloads
Require a human review step before passing A output to B
Restrict B to structured inputs only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and requests API keys/environment variables; Agent B has broad network egress and a REST API. If they share a workspace or credentials, A’s sensitive inputs could be exposed through B’s outbound calls. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace or mounted files
IF Agent B receives any of Agent A’s document contents or secrets
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Remove secrets from Agent A’s runtime unless required
Block outbound network from B except approved endpoints
Redact documents before cross-agent transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A supports multiple instances and can write via document-processing workflows; Agent B exposes a REST API but no write scopes or mutable-resource permissions are listed. Without evidence of shared writable state, direct capability conflict is limited and likely requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or document set
IF an external orchestrator does not serialize updates
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make B read-only unless explicitly needed
Use per-agent branches or copies
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and Agent B is an evaluation/observability tool that may consume outputs from other systems. If B treats A’s generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream reports or actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Agent B ingests A-generated diagrams or text without validation
IF downstream users act on B’s rendered conclusions as factual
mitigations: Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Require B to cite source documents separately
Add a verification checklist before downstream use
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A explicitly handles API keys and document files, while Agent B’s profile shows no sensitive data classes or residency constraints. A compliance mismatch is possible only if regulated data is routed into B, but the profiles do not document such a flow, so the risk is limited and one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound data is routed from Agent A into Agent B
IF retention or logging policies differ for the same document set
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Document retention settings for both agents
Disable unnecessary logging on both sides
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
